belief: I earned everything; others just didn't try.
origins: A family that prized hard work, a career that rewarded effort, or a community that looked down on struggle can teach us that success is simply the result of trying. Because effort really does matter, the belief feels true. What it leaves out is the help, health, timing, opportunity, and gifts that came from outside us, and the hardships other people carry that we cannot see.
teaches: Scripture honors diligence. Proverbs says diligent hands bring profit. But Scripture also says that every good gift comes from God, and Moses warned Israel not to say, “The power and strength of my hands have made this wealth for me,” because it is the Lord who gives the power to gain wealth. Paul asks, “What do you have that you did not receive?” These passages do not tell us to feel guilty for working hard or for having something. They invite thankfulness, humility, and open hands toward those who have less.
self_statements: Anyone who really tried would have what I have.
People who struggle brought it on themselves.
I did this on my own.
I do not owe anyone anything.
If they wanted it, they would have worked harder.
Being generous would only reward laziness.
errors: Crediting my results to effort alone and other people’s results to their flaws.
Believing that people either earn what they have or deserve what they lack.
Remembering my effort and overlooking the help, health, and opportunities I received.
Judging everyone who struggles by what I assume about a few.
questions: What help, timing, health, or opportunity did I receive that I did not earn?
Who taught me, hired me, or gave me a chance?
What hidden burdens could someone else be carrying that I cannot see?
What do I have that I did not receive?
How would my view of others change if I held success more loosely?
What is one way I can use what I have to bless someone else?
truth: Effort matters, and I can be glad about work well done. But everything I have, including my health, my abilities, and my opportunities, came through God’s hand and the help of others. I can be thankful instead of proud, and generous instead of judging.
hw_truths: Hard work matters, and so does grace.
Everything I have is a gift to be stewarded.
I do not know what others carry.
God, not my effort, gives the power to get wealth.
I can honor my work and still stay humble.
log: Each evening, write one thing today that came from someone else’s help or from God’s provision, and one thing you did yourself.
actions: List five gifts you did not earn.
Include people who helped you, abilities you were born with, and opportunities that came your way.
Write or say a specific thank-you to one person who made a difference in your path.
Ask a question instead of making a judgment.
Next time you assume someone “just didn’t try,” ask a kind question about their story and listen.
Choose an amount you are comfortable with and give it to someone in need, quietly.
prayer: Father, every good gift comes from You. Forgive me for the pride that says I did it all myself. Make me thankful, humble, and generous toward people who carry burdens I cannot see. Amen.
hw_questions: What did I receive that I did not earn?
Who helped me along the way?
What might this person be carrying that I cannot see?
What would thankfulness look like today?
How can I use what I have to help someone?
Where has pride shaped how I see others?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God gives me the power to work, so I can be thankful, humble, and generous.”
